endorsements.quote: If an available external test set exists that represents the target population, it should be tested as part of the model development process to ensure that the NLP tool is portable and externally valid.
It is important for models to be evaluated continually to determine whether they should be fine-tuned and updated, and whether any biases exist.
Validation of NLP models is key both retrospectively and prospectively, as data change longitudinally.

unlisted_practices: Assess data readiness of clinical text corpora, including plausibility, conformance, and completeness of notes and metadata, before starting an NLP project.
Ensure infrastructure exists at the design phase so NLP systems can be operationally tested, translated to production, and maintained.
Confirm the NLP tool addresses a known, high-priority clinical need and is aligned with organizational incentives and clinical leadership priorities before development.
Involve clinicians, clinical informaticians, and health care administrators from the start of NLP projects and integrate stakeholders into the software development life cycle.
Develop a business plan and strategy for maintaining deployed NLP models to sustain clinical application.
Include different note types in the training corpus when the target corpus spans multiple note types.
Evaluate NLP performance at the mention, document, or patient level as appropriate to the clinical use, rather than only at the text level.
Require performance metric reporting for all NLP tools intended to be transportable outside their training corpus.
Customize NLP systems developed at other institutions to the local data set through specific preprocessing steps.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint paper outlining practical considerations and recommendations for developing and maintaining clinical NLP systems in healthcare organizations.
